statement_record.book: Given F : C → D, G : D → C and a family of bijections D(Fc,d) ≅ C(c,Gd) NOT assumed natural, naturality of the family is EQUIVALENT to: for all h : c' → c, k : d → d', f♯ : Fc → d, g♯ : Fc' → d', the square (Fh, f♯, g♯, k) commutes in D if and only if the transposed square (h, f♭, g♭, Gk) commutes in C. Separately the two naturality directions say that the transpose of k ∘ f♯ is Gk ∘ f♭ and the transpose of f♯ ∘ Fh is f♭ ∘ h.

statement_record.book: An adjunction between preorders is called a (monotone) Galois connection: since functors between preorders are exactly order-preserving functions (Exercise 1.3.ii), an adjunction F ⊣ G between order-preserving F : A → B and G : B → A asserts precisely that F a ≤ b if and only if a ≤ G b, for all a ∈ A, b ∈ B. F is the lower adjoint, G the upper adjoint.
statement_record.intree: The two halves exist separately: `Proset (P : PreOrder R) : Category` with `hom := R` and a trivially-true hom-setoid, and `Class Adjunction` over arbitrary categories. Nothing in tree instantiates the second at the first, names the result, or states the biconditional.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the specialization would be definitional (Proset's hom is the relation itself and its setoid identifies all proofs, so `Adjunction (Proset P) (Proset Q) F G` unfolds to exactly the pair of implications F a ≤ b → a ≤ G b and a ≤ G b → F a ≤ b, with naturality vacuous), but the library never performs it: no definition, no lemma, no instance.

evidence.intree_statement: Class LeftKan := { Lan : [A, C] ⟶ [B, C]; lan_adjoint : Lan ⊣ Induced }.  — the left adjoint of restriction along F : A ⟶ B (the book's induction ind ⊣ res).
Class RightKan := { Ran : [A, C] ⟶ [B, C]; ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran }.  — the right adjoint of the same restriction functor (the book's coinduction res ⊣ coind).

Program Definition Induced : ([B, C]) ⟶ ([A, C]) := {| fobj := fun G => G ◯ F; fmap := fun _ _ f => {| transform := fun z => transform[f] (F z) |} |}.  — restriction (precomposition) along F, the functor of which the two adjoints above are taken; specializing F := Bφ and A := BH, B := BG gives exactly the book's φ*.

statement_record.book: For any complete and cocomplete category C and any group homomorphism φ : H → G, the restriction functor φ* : C^{BG} → C^{BH} admits both a left and a right adjoint (proved in Example 6.2.9). For a subgroup inclusion H ⊆ G these are induction ind^G_H and coinduction coind^G_H, so ind ⊣ res ⊣ coind. Taking C = Vect_k, the adjunction ind^G_H ⊣ res^G_H between H- and G-representations is Frobenius reciprocity.
statement_record.intree: Class LeftKan := { Lan : [A,C] ⟶ [B,C]; lan_adjoint : Lan ⊣ Induced } and Class RightKan := { Ran : [A,C] ⟶ [B,C]; ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran }, over Induced := (− ◯ F) : [B,C] ⟶ [A,C].
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on two counts. (1) EXISTENCE IS ASSUMED, NOT PROVED: LeftKan and RightKan are hypothesis classes; the library proves no theorem producing them from cocompleteness/completeness of C (Riehl's Example 6.2.9 / §6.2), and no concrete instance of either class exists in the tree (the only consumer, Structure/Limit/Kan/Extension.v:46 `Kan_Limit`, takes `{@RightKan _ _ (Erase J) C}` as a hypothesis too). (2) The general form is stated for restriction along an arbitrary functor F : A ⟶ B and so subsumes the book's φ* only after an instantiation that cannot be written, since none of BG, C^{BG}, group homomorphisms, or Vect_k exists in tree.
